clue.text: Disguise unpleasant medicine that can make pulse alright

indicators.note: the letters of pulse and alright can be made into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remedy that will put your heartbeat right, if you can stomach it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that can make' is the anagram signal: PULSE plus ALRIGHT, twelve letters, rearranged give the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make something unwelcome more palatable, as coating a bitter tablet does.

clue.text: Part of notice's spoilt

indicators.note: a spoilt thing is ruined and disordered, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

parts.note: the possessive gives its S as a letter here: NOTICE plus S

explanation.surface: Some of a public notice has been defaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoilt' signals rearranging NOTICES, with the 's counted as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a portion or division of a whole, a synonym for a part.

clue.text: Annoyance starts to get really intense, exacerbating feelings

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters, one from each

explanation.surface: Irritation builds as emotions grow fiercer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes the first letter of each of the five words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief in the informal sense of trouble or hassle, as in 'giving someone grief', is annoyance.

clue.text: New prince's traditional tone?

parts.note: a baby boy is traditionally dressed in a pale shade, and a baby prince is regal, so his colour combines the two ideas

explanation.surface: What colour should a newborn heir to the throne wear?
explanation.walkthrough: Baby boys are traditionally put in blue; a royal baby boy gets the royal shade of it. The question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep, vivid shade, here imagined as the colour fitting a royal newborn boy.

clue.text: Appropriate greeting to sailor

parts.note: hi is a casual greeting
Jack, or jack tar, is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Saying hello is the right way to address a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like the adjective 'suitable' but is the verb 'take for oneself'.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack something is to seize or take it over, which is to appropriate it.

clue.text: Primitive mammal of a kind lacking tail and covering

indicators.note: covering means the first piece wraps round the letters that follow it

parts.note: plus means and, as in two plus two

indicators.note: the word for kind loses its final letter, its tail

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort

explanation.surface: A primitive creature of a sort that has no tail and no coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' hides as a piece: its synonym is the container. 'lacking tail' leaves TYP, and with A it sits inside, which 'covering' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed platypus is an egg-laying monotreme, regarded as one of the most primitive living mammals.

clue.text: Look round only outside of priory? That's stupid

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
O is round in shape

indicators.note: only the outside of the word is used: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Glancing about the edge of a monastery is a daft thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only outside of' keeps P and Y, the first and last letters of priory.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy is informal for crazy or silly, so it means foolish.

clue.text: Europeans holding two kings — second is black

indicators.note: holding means the first word wraps round the letters given next

parts.note: Danes are people from Denmark, so Europeans
R (Latin rex) and K (chess) are both abbreviations for king
R (Latin rex) and K (chess) are both abbreviations for king

explanation.surface: A group of continental people with a couple of monarchs; the next one is dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts R and K inside DANES to make DARKNES; S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkness is blackness, the absence of light; 'black' used as a noun means the same.

clue.text: Put up extremely short enclosure inside for cat

indicators.note: inside means the shortened word sits within the other piece
in a down clue, put up means the word is written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: too means extremely, as in 'too kind'

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a cell is a small enclosed room

explanation.surface: Raise a pen that is far too small inside, to house the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' gives OOT, and 'short' leaves CEL, which 'inside' places in the middle. 'Put up' reads as 'erect' but reverses in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a wild spotted feline of the Americas, a kind of cat.

clue.text: Chase girl behind church

indicators.note: behind means the girl's name follows the church abbreviation

parts.note: Ivy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Pursue the young woman who trails after the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' sets the girl's name after the church; 'Chase' is a verb here, not the bank or a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To chivy (or chivvy) is to hound or harass someone, originally to pursue in a hunt.

clue.text: French maid Shaw put on the stage

definitions.meaning: the Maid of Orléans, the French heroine who led troops in the Hundred Years War
George Bernard Shaw dramatised her life in his play Saint Joan

explanation.surface: A French servant appeared in a production by the playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French maid' suggests a servant in a farce, but is the medieval saint, subject of Shaw's play Saint Joan.
explanation.definitionFit: She is known as the Maid of Orléans, a French saint whose story Shaw staged.

clue.text: Closely pursuing, complete with hawk

parts.note: in full means completely, with nothing left out
to hawk wares is to cry them out for sale

explanation.surface: Total, plus a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hawk' looks like the bird but is the verb meaning to peddle by calling out, CRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes hounds baying together while hot on the scent, so chasing hard.

clue.text: Peasant discovers two oxen left behind

indicators.note: behind places the letter for left after the pair of oxen

parts.note: a yoke is a pair of oxen harnessed together

explanation.surface: A farmer finds his pair of draught animals has been left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' puts L after YOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated country person, a rustic.

clue.text: Provoke intense rivalry

definitions.meaning: to irritate or goad someone deliberately
bad feeling between competitors, as in a grudge match

explanation.definitionFit: To needle is to goad; in sport, needle also means hostility between rivals.

clue.text: Large exhibition certainly produces media coverage

parts.note: an expo is a large public exhibition or trade fair
sure means certainly, as in 'sure, I'll come'

explanation.surface: A big trade show is guaranteed to attract the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produces' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure means publicity, the amount of attention given in the press and broadcasting.

clue.text: Cite religious writing about one result of division

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go round the letter for one

parts.note: to quote is to cite words from a source
I is the Roman numeral for one
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: Refer to scripture on the subject of unity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the cited word plus the scripture round the Roman one, which lands between its T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, the quotient is the number got by dividing one number by another.

clue.text: Immediately after that, he threw it out

indicators.note: out means the preceding words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: He promptly tossed it away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals rearranging HE THREW IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Therewith is an old adverb meaning straight after that, thereupon.

clue.text: It takes fifty grand to incarcerate one criminal until death

indicators.note: to incarcerate is to lock up, so the first pair of letters encloses the next pieces

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
I is the Roman numeral for one
a felon is a criminal

explanation.surface: Locking up an offender costs fifty thousand, for the rest of his life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to incarcerate' puts I plus FELON between L and G. 'It takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifelong describes something lasting a whole lifetime, that is, right up to the end.

clue.text: Marx dropping round by river, returned in aircraft

indicators.note: dropping round means losing the ring-shaped letter O

parts.note: Zeppo was the youngest of the Marx Brothers comedy team

indicators.note: returned means the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: A Marx brother pops round, then comes back by river in a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping round' removes the brother's O and 'returned' turns the river round; Marx suggests Karl, but it is Zeppo of the comedy brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: A zeppelin is a rigid airship, a kind of lighter-than-air craft.

clue.text: Spot the lady's instrument

parts.note: a zit is a pimple or spot
her, as in her instrument, belonging to the lady

explanation.surface: Notice the woman's musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like the verb 'notice' but is a pimple.
explanation.definitionFit: The zither is a stringed musical instrument played flat, plucked with the fingers.

clue.text: Sly person getting wide support for artist

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide, a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach
an easel holds a painter's canvas

explanation.surface: A cunning type obtains a broad stand for a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel, figuratively, is a deceitful or treacherous individual.

clue.text: Those first in Yukon and Alaska got in the money, truly

indicators.note: got in means the picked letters are placed within the word for money

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money

indicators.note: the first letters in each of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: Early arrivals in the far north struck it rich, honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those first in' gives Y and A, which 'got in' sets after the second letter of the money word.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyally means faithfully, which is one sense of truly, as in 'yours truly'.

clue.text: See me after fatty stuff upped weight

indicators.note: after means the word me comes after the reversed spread
in a down clue, upped means the word is written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: marg is short for margarine, a fatty spread

explanation.surface: Look, I've put on weight after eating fatty food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upped' gives GRAM in a down clue; 'after' sets the second piece behind it. 'See' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramme (gram) is a metric unit of mass, a small weight.

clue.text: Sample some ragout (a stew)

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Try a little of the stew.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across ragouT A STEw.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste food is to try a little of it, so to sample it.

clue.text: Lower, less nitrogen — higher, clear air

indicators.note: less means a letter is taken away from the word for lower

parts.note: nether means lower, as in the nether regions
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A contrast between the lower atmosphere, short of a gas, and the clear upper air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes N from NETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetically the ether is the clear sky, the upper regions of the atmosphere above the clouds.

clue.text: Zealously arriving too soon, going round home

indicators.note: going round means the first word encloses the next

parts.note: early means ahead of time
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Eagerly getting in ahead of time, circling the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' has the word for ahead of time wrap the bird's home; 'arriving too soon' looks like part of the definition but is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnestly means with serious, intense conviction, which is close to fervently.

clue.text: In Belgian port you'll not find an idiot

indicators.note: you'll not find means the word an is missing from the port's name

parts.note: Antwerp is the major port of Belgium

explanation.surface: Fools are scarce in a Flemish harbour city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you'll not find' takes AN off ANTWERP. 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly, foolish person, a nitwit.

clue.text: Something found in the soil damaged the marrow

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A pest in the vegetable patch has spoiled the squash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' signals rearranging THE MARROW. Marrow is a large British garden squash.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthworm is a creature that burrows through the ground.

clue.text: One understanding what's best

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a deal is an understanding or agreement

explanation.surface: One who comprehends the optimum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'understanding' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The ideal is the perfect standard, the most desirable option.

clue.text: Oilman on time, pleased to be quick on the draw

indicators.note: on means the oilman comes after, written onto, the letter for time

parts.note: a rigger works on an oil rig
happy means pleased

explanation.surface: A rig worker, glad to be punctual, is fast with a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts RIGGER after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Trigger-happy describes someone too ready to fire a gun, which is being too fast to draw.
